text:
maya: starting a perf sweep for silverfin-3b as a candidate for our int4 lineup. goal: find sweet spot for batching and ctx that meets p50 < 120ms for 512 tokens and throughput > 800 tok/s on p4d-test.
liam: 👍 which quant configs are we testing first? int4 pure, int8 fallback, and fp16 baseline?
maya: exactly. prioritized: int4 w/ fp16 fallback, int8 calibrated, then fp16. also run KV-cache sanity for chat workloads.
rahul: queued on p4d-test. I’ll run ctx sweep 512/1024/2048 and batch sizes 1/2/4/8. putting perf-bot on the thread for logs.
perf-bot: queued job 84321 on runner p4d-test. ETA ~3.5h. will post artifacts to https://s3.redwood-internal/bench/84321/ when done.
eva: quick ask — are we running with continuous batching enabled? that changes p95 a lot.
maya: yes, run both with `--continuous_batching` on/off so we can see latency SLO tradeoffs. include tokenization warmup of 10 steps.
liam: added evaluation prompt set (regression-set-v2) to the artifact list. want QA on quality regressions before approving int4.
rahul: first run finished (512 ctx, batch 1, int4). perf-bot attached summary.
perf-bot: artifact: https://s3.redwood-internal/bench/84321/summary.json
maya: paste of key lines from summary:
```
config: silverfin-3b int4, ctx=512, batch=1
throughput: 920 tok/s
latency p50: 115 ms
latency p95: 420 ms
mem: 18.2 GB GPU
quality: chr_f1 delta vs fp16: -0.9% (regression-set-v2)
```
liam: promising on p50, p95 is high but expected for batch=1. how does batch=4 look?
rahul: batch=4, ctx=512, int4: throughput 2200 tok/s, p50 260 ms, p95 580 ms. memory 20.5 GB.
eva: important to note: continuous_batching on produced p95 330 ms at batch=1 for same config (kept tail low). worth considering for hosted routes.
maya: noted. can we get ctx=2048 numbers? that's our conservative target for some customers.
perf-bot: running job 84322 (ctx=2048, batch sweep).
rahul: ctx=2048 results (int4): batch=1 throughput 680 tok/s, p50 170 ms, p95 720 ms, mem 21.9 GB. batch=2 throughput 1300 tok/s p50 210 ms p95 680 ms.
liam: so int4 at 2048 barely meets throughput target for batch 1, better with batch 2. quality delta worsened a bit?
maya: quality: for ctx=2048 int4, chr_f1 delta -1.6% vs fp16. int8 showed -0.3%.
eva: suggestion: offer int4 for low-ctx/high-batch routes, int8 for high-ctx/low-latency routes. document fallback in model config.
maya: agreed. also found a micro-regression in stop-sequence handling in int4 samples — logging issue #CAM-111. pinging inference-team.
liam: can we get a quick smoke with `--kv_cache=true` and a streaming response path? prod behavior matters.
rahul: ran kv_cache smoke for int4, ctx=1024, batch=1 streaming: p50 130ms, p95 410ms, no OOMs. some tokenization mismatch in 0.2% of samples, capturing examples in artifacts.
maya: ok capture those examples and add to eval runbook. also add canary rollout plan: 5% traffic int4 -> monitor token-level diffs and latency. rollback triggers: chr_f1 drop >1.5% or p95 increase >200ms.
eha: (joined) what about scheduling and GPU allocation? do we need a dedicated pool to stabilize p95?
maya: for initial canary use dedicated small pool (dedicated-gold-1) for predictability. if stable, move to shared pool with autoscale heuristics.
liam: will prepare PR for model catalog entry and include perf knobs: batching_policy, continuous_batching_enabled, fallback_model: silverfin-3b-fp16, quant_profile: int4-2026-05-calib.
rahul: final note: fp16 baseline numbers: ctx=512 batch=1 throughput 980 tok/s p50 105ms p95 360ms. int8 is very close to fp16 in quality and latency.
maya: thanks all — next steps: 1) liam submits catalog PR, 2) eva drafts canary runbook + metric dashboards, 3) rahul schedules canary and attaches artifacts. will reconvene after canary results. :thumbsup:
